```data
orchestrator/jev_gate.py:406 The new `if economy and not ambiguous: return finish(None)` short-circuit runs before the existing `mode == "block" and cfg.get("block_repeats") and repeat` check. Once block_repeats is flipped to true (or set true per-task), repeated identical Read/Grep/Glob calls will silently stop being blocked, contradicting the spec's explicit 'do not touch the block path' instruction. This is confirmed by the diff itself: tests/test_jev_gate.py::test_block_repeats_denies was changed from the suite's default Read tool_name to `tool_name="Bash"` specifically so the test keeps passing -- i.e. the regression was worked around in the test rather than fixed or called out.
orchestrator/jev_gate.py:364 When mode=="block", block_repeats=true and an *ambiguous* economy call (e.g. repeated_read_changed/narrower_search) also has repeat=True, the block path logs via a direct `_log(...)` call rather than `finish(...)`, so `economy=` is never passed and the gate.jsonl row omits read_kind/tokens_estimate/would_suppress. Spec item 2 asks every classified Read/Grep/Glob call to log those fields; this reachable edge case silently drops them.
```

Planner note: both comments are right. (1) In jev_gate the economy short-circuit for unambiguous kinds must run AFTER the existing block_repeats check (when mode == block and block_repeats and repeat, that path stays authoritative); first reads still skip the Jev sample. (2) The block path logs through finish(...) (or passes economy= to _log) so read_kind, tokens_estimate and would_suppress land in every classified row. Add tests/test_jev_gate.py::test_block_repeats_still_reaches_block_path_with_economy and ::test_block_path_row_carries_economy_fields.
